extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers and policymakers interested in African exploration, colonial expeditions, and public education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for organizing and judging expeditions into the interior of Africa (seasonality, force composition, conduct toward natives, evidence assessment) and for assessing the effectiveness of public education, as discussed in a historical/biographical essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Season/timing for expedition departure
rubrics_metrics.description: The season in which an expedition sets out is decisive for success; Park's failure was 'entirely owing to the improper season at which his journey was undertaken.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer sailing from England before October and being ready to depart the Gambia by the end of November; from that time there is 'an uninterrupted continuance of fine and healthy weather during a period of five months.' Delays that push the journey into the rainy season greatly increase sickness and loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a military escort
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an expedition should be accompanied by a military escort is a central practical question; the text concludes that a military plan is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A properly organized military escort (limited to security/protection purposes) affords more ample means of observation and enquiry, inspires respect among Africans, supports friendly and commercial intercourse, and reduces risks compared with solitary or unprotected individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and source of troops
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of troops drawn from local/enlisted populations (specifically the Royal African corps at Sierra Leone) is proposed as a basis for expeditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use well-trained black troops from Sierra Leone who are inured to the climate, accustomed to hardships, capable of exertion, and attached to the British Government. These troops are praised for obedience, steadiness, and general good conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership structure and delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: An expedition should have a clear command structure with qualified deputies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appoint a person with immediate command and one or two other leading persons 'each properly qualified to assist in the direction and management of the principal concerns, and (in case of emergency) to undertake the sole charge of the expedition.' Leaders should be able to detach small parties taking distinct lines of march as circumstances require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Force size and logistical constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of troops must be balanced against probable means of subsistence and logistical realities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulate troop numbers with 'due regard to the probable means of subsistence' so the detachment is sufficiently numerous for security but sustainable in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct toward natives: strict avoidance of aggression
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders are to be enjoined to avoid all acts of aggression and to abstain from violence except in absolute self-defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official instructions should direct leaders 'to use his utmost endeavours to establish a friendly intercourse and communication with the inhabitants' and to employ interpreters and black troops as 'messengers of peace and conciliation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of interpreters and local agents for diplomacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ the most intelligent of the black troops as interpreters and emissaries to foster peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreters drawn from the expedition's troops facilitate friendly relations and communication; using local or culturally appropriate intermediaries is emphasized as a diplomatic necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel selection for solitary or caravan travel
rubrics_metrics.description: When sending single individuals on journeys, prefer Muslim (Mahometan) travellers or suitable natives who can accompany caravans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If solitary exploration continues, it may be better to employ 'Mahometan travellers' or natives from regions like Hindostan who can travel with established caravans, thereby reducing dangers Europeans face among certain groups (e.g., Moors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against abuses in recruiting enlistees
rubrics_metrics.description: While enlisting captured Africans into troops can be beneficial, the practice is 'liable to some abuse' and requires oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative wisdom and rigorous investigation of charges of misconduct should be applied; let not occasional abuses be argued as valid objections to the practice if, on balance, it benefits the Africans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generalizing from extreme or accidental failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not draw sweeping negative conclusions about expeditions from singular disastrous cases (e.g., Park's death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extreme cases or accidents (like the death of a leader) do not determine overall feasibility; reasonable and sufficient inducements may remain for attempting further discoveries, and proper organization can supply prior defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical aims and measures of a successful expedition
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal objects are geographical discovery, ascertaining the Niger's course and termination, understanding inhabitants' conditions, and collecting commercial and improvement data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct enquiries with attention to friendly intercourse, avoidance of aggression, adequate security, interpreters, and proper seasonality to maximize chances of success and beneficial consequences (trade, knowledge, civilization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of documentary evidence and testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the authenticity and reliability of translated native journals and single-informant accounts carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider translation quality ('translated by some person who probably had but a moderate knowledge'), internal clarity, corroboration by other circumstances, the lengthy lapse of time without intelligence, the informant's credibility and motives, and the difference between hearsay and direct testimony. Translation errors and theatrical or improbable details should be treated skeptically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traits of a good traveller/explorer
rubrics_metrics.description: Key personal qualities that made Park notable: enterprising spirit, indefatigable vigilance and activity, calm fortitude, unshaken perseverance, correctness of judgment, solidity rather than brilliance, attention to facts, and avoidance of exaggeration or credulity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such character traits are 'peculiarly suited to a traveller and geographical discoverer' and enable consistent, rational accounts free from enthusiasm or speculative hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of an effective system of public education (Scotland example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful public instruction system is legally established, widely accessible (schools in every parish), connected with local ecclesiastical structures, and practically regulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Scottish model: statute provisions (1646, re-enacted 1696) establishing parish schools 'for the express purpose of teaching the poor,' supported by acts of Church Assemblies forming a practical code; where parishes are large, private subscriptions supplement parochial seminaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes/metrics of successful education
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure an education system's success by social effects: reduction in crimes, widespread habits of industry and frugality, social mobility, family progress, and general intelligence/farsightedness among the lower classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include low executions per year, the prevalence of professional advancement (e.g., gardeners), parental pride in children's advancement, and broad civilizing effects—education is credited as 'by far the most important' cause of such changes.
